proposal.thesis: DexCom reported Q2 2026 results on 2026-07-30 and raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $5.18-5.25B (8-K/earnings release 2026-07-30), driven by expanded Type 2 diabetes access -- a real, dated, bundle-sourced catalyst. The fresh XBRL ratios show genuine quality improvement, not just top-line growth: gross margin 63.44% vs 59.53% a year ago (Q ended 2026-06-30), operating margin 24.33% vs 18.37% a year ago, and TTM free cash flow +146.1% YoY, alongside a shrinking share count from net buybacks. The stock confirmed a breakout above its 20-day high one session ago, sits at a fresh 52-week high with weekly higher-highs/higher-lows and a rising 30-week MA, and institutional ownership-flow sponsorship (institutions_buying_price_rising) corroborates the move. It is 6 days past its print -- squarely inside the preferred post-print-drift lane (binary resolved, geometry clean) -- reports again 2026-10-29 (85 days out, no blackout risk), and its healthcare/ai_neutral demand driver is genuinely orthogonal to this book's only other holding (BKR, energy), making this a real diversification add rather than a second helping of the same factor bet.

This book's own 9-name universe subset shows broad participation (100% above 200-DMA, 100% beating SPY 1m) -- an AI/tech-biased sample, not literal market breadth, but directionally supportive. proposal.risk_map: The clearest ways this fails: (1) inventory is building faster than revenue (55.52% of quarterly revenue vs 49.32% a year ago per the XBRL ratios) -- if that reflects slower Type 2 sell-through rather than pre-launch stocking, the growth thesis cracks; (2) the stock is only one session past its breakout anchor and 1% off its 52-week high, so a failed follow-through or gap-fill is a real near-term risk, against a macro backdrop carrying some risk-off tape chatter today (Michael Burry '1987-style crash' comment, MarketWatch); (3) options positioning reads mixed/neutral with no strong derivatives confirmation either way; (4) sector_comps coverage for this name is thin in this run's scan (only 1 healthcare peer scanned), so a quantitative 'cheap vs sector' claim cannot be verified this run and is not being made. Early tell: a daily close back below the anchored VWAP (~$86.50) on above-average volume, giving back the 7/30 post-earnings gap.
proposal.variant_perception: CONSENSUS: 25 analysts carry a strong_buy rating with a mean target of $93.44, only +7.5% above last close -- Street has given some credit to the beat-and-raise but is anchored close to the current print. MY VIEW: the raised FY2026 guide driven by expanded Type 2 diabetes access is a durable TAM expansion, not a one-quarter pop, and margins are expanding faster than a single-name target of +7.5% implies -- operating margin +5.96pp YoY and FCF nearly doubling are not fully reflected in a target this close to spot. MECHANISM: this print is only 6 days old, so out-year sell-side models likely have not yet rolled the Type 2 diabetes access expansion into their growth assumptions; the market is pricing DXCM as a steady-state medtech grower (fwd P/E 32.8x on 12.2% forward growth) rather than an accelerating share-gain story, which is what the margin trend and guide raise actually describe. RESOLUTION: the next data point is Q3 2026 commentary or interim sell-through data on Type 2 uptake over the next 2-4 weeks, followed by the scheduled 2026-10-29 print.

thesis_invalidators.invalidating_structure: A daily close back below the anchored VWAP / breakout level near $86.50 on above-average volume, giving back the 2026-07-30 post-earnings gap.
thesis_invalidators.time_box: If DXCM has not sustained a daily close above $92 (clearing the current $93.44 analyst mean target zone and confirming trend continuation) within 25 trading days of entry, exit and rotate -- a one-session-old breakout needs follow-through, not just a held gap.
